title: Optimizing Speculative Decoding for Serving Large Language Models Using Goodput (SmartSpec)
quote: under higher request rates or low speculation accuracy, it paradoxically increases latency
proves: In vLLM with continuous batching, fixed speculation can raise latency under high load; SmartSpec picks a per-request length from 0 (spec off) to many tokens by estimating goodput, cutting average latency up to 3.2x vs no spec.
does_not_prove: Goodput model is per step and per request; does not account for draft KV memory reducing admitted batch, preemption, or chunked-prefill sharing. v1 results superseded by v3 (B2).
bearing: Supports per-request spec on/off as known territory; threatens any 'adaptive K by load' novelty claim.

title: TurboSpec: Closed-loop Speculation Control System for Optimizing LLM Serving Goodput
quote: automatically profiles the execution environment
proves: SmartSpec v3 renamed TurboSpec: offline profiling plus online feedback picks speculation level maximizing predicted goodput in vLLM; claims consistent gains across workloads and hardware.
does_not_prove: No venue listed; abstract gives no number; controller targets speculation level only, not admission or memory split between draft state and target KV.
bearing: Threatens closed-loop K controller ideas; leaves memory-aware admission open.

title: Speculative Decoding: Performance or Illusion?
venue: arXiv preprint (v2 Mar 2026; MLSys 2026 per search, venue not on abs page)
quote: the speedup of EAGLE over the non-SD baseline decreases from 1.73x to 1.21x as the batch size increases from 1 to 128
proves: In vLLM, EAGLE speedup on Llama3.1-8B GSM8K falls 1.73x to 1.21x from batch 1 to batch 128; verification is 42-95% of runtime; oracle adaptive combinations show up to 2.2x further headroom over the best fixed strategy.
does_not_prove: Oracle headroom ignores predictor cost and EAGLE KV maintenance; paper does not report its own crossover batch where SD is slower; quote has 'x' for the times sign.
bearing: Negative/workload result: shrinks gains at high batch size; supports a lightweight per-position predictor gap.

title: MagicDec: Breaking the Latency-Throughput Tradeoff for Long Context Generation with Speculative Decoding
venue: arXiv preprint (v5 Apr 2025; ICLR 2025 per search)
quote: Speculative decoding (SD) is a widely used technique to reduce latency losslessly
proves: At moderate-to-long contexts the KV cache dominates step cost, so SD with a sparse-KV draft still speeds up batch 32-256 serving (up to 2.51x Llama3.1-8B).
does_not_prove: Gain depends on long context where the target is memory-bound on KV; says nothing about short-context high batch or admission control; abs page lists no venue.
bearing: Supports long-context exception to 'spec hurts at high batch'; threatens claims that high batch always kills SD.

title: EAGLE-3: Scaling up Inference Acceleration of Large Language Models via Training-Time Test
quote: EAGLE reduces throughput at a batch size of 24
proves: In SGLang on H100 Llama3.1-8B MT-Bench, EAGLE is 0.93x at batch 24 while EAGLE-3 is 1.38x at batch 64; in vLLM EAGLE drops to 0.71x at batch 56 and EAGLE-3 to 1.01x.
does_not_prove: Short context, single model, one dataset; hardware labeling inconsistent (RTX3090 vs A100); no scheduler-level adaptation.
bearing: Negative result: concrete crossover batch where spec turns into slowdown.

title: AdaServe: Accelerating Multi-SLO LLM Serving with SLO-Customized Speculative Decoding
quote: reduces SLO violations by up to 4.3x and improves goodput
proves: Builds a per-request speculation tree sized to each request's latency SLO with a speculate-select-verify pipeline; up to 4.3x fewer SLO violations and 1.9x goodput vs best baselines.
does_not_prove: Per-step token allocation, not admission control; does not model draft KV memory or preemption cost; 'x' substituted for times sign in quote.
bearing: Threatens SLO-aware per-request spec budget ideas.

title: SpecServe: Efficient and SLO-Aware Large Language Model Serving with Adaptive Speculative Decoding (v2 retitled AdaSpec)
quote: existing speculative decoding solutions often fail to adapt to varying workloads and system environments
proves: Adjusts speculation strategy to real-time load with a theoretical efficiency model; claims 1.14x-14.3x over SOTA speculative systems while meeting SLOs.
does_not_prove: The 14.3x upper figure is dropped from v2; baseline choice unclear from abstract.
bearing: Threatens load-adaptive SLO-aware spec ideas.

title: SpecDec++: Boosting Speculative Decoding via Adaptive Candidate Lengths
quote: Our adaptive method achieves a 2.04x speedup on the Alpaca dataset
proves: Trained acceptance-prediction head with threshold stop rule (MDP-optimal); 2.04x on Alpaca, only 7.2% over fixed-K baseline (9.4% GSM8K, 11.1% HumanEval).
does_not_prove: Batch size 1 style evaluation, single 7B/70B pair; no serving batch effects.
bearing: Negative-ish: per-request adaptive K gives roughly 7-11% over tuned fixed K.

title: Dynamic Speculation Lookahead Accelerates Speculative Decoding of Large Language Models (DISCO)
venue: arXiv preprint (v5 Nov 2024; NeurIPS 2024 ENLSP workshop per search)
quote: DISCO reaches an average speedup of 10% compared to the best static SL baseline
proves: A classifier choosing speculation length per iteration gives about 10% average over the best static length, output identical.
does_not_prove: Single-request setting; no batching or serving load.
bearing: Negative result: dynamic length gain over best static is small (~10%).

title: AdaEDL: Early Draft Stopping for Speculative Decoding of Large Language Models via an Entropy-based Lower Bound on Token Acceptance Probability
quote: other training-free draft-stopping techniques by upto 10% in a variety of settings and datasets
proves: Training-free entropy-based draft stop beats static draft length by 10-57% and other training-free stoppers by up to 10%.
does_not_prove: Gains largest when drafting is expensive; no batch-level or server-load evaluation.
bearing: Shows per-request stop rules are crowded and the margin among them is small.

title: BanditSpec: Adaptive Speculative Decoding via Bandit Algorithms
quote: the throughput is close to the oracle best hyperparameter
proves: UCB/EXP3 bandits choose spec hyperparameters online, training-free, with regret bounds; throughput near the oracle-best fixed hyperparameter in simulated serving.
does_not_prove: 'Close to oracle best fixed' implies adaptive selection mostly recovers the best static choice rather than beating it; serving is simulated.
bearing: Negative-ish: bounds the value of online K selection to about the best fixed K.

title: Nightjar: Dynamic Adaptive Speculative Decoding for Large Language Models Serving
quote: offloads the draft model to the CPU only under GPU memory pressure
proves: Bandit planner picks K per batch size, disables spec under high load, and offloads the draft to CPU to reclaim KV for larger batches; up to 14.76% throughput and 20.18% lower latency vs standard SD; defines C_switch as KV-reconstruction overhead of re-enabling spec.
does_not_prove: Small consumer/datacenter GPUs and small drafts; says restart cost of speculation was previously unquantified; does not study preemption interaction.
bearing: Closest prior art to memory-aware admission with draft overhead and spec on/off switching cost; threatens that candidate.

title: Adaptive verification (vLLM docs)
quote: the highest-scoring slots are admitted until a global budget is spent
proves: vLLM ranks every (request, position) draft slot by survival probability across the batch and admits slots up to a global token budget chosen by startup profiling to maximize accepted tokens per second.
does_not_prove: No numbers on the page; needs a confidence head and full cudagraphs; not with LoRA or pipeline parallelism; budget is per step, not tied to admission or prefill.
bearing: Threatens cross-request verification-budget allocation ideas; it is in upstream vLLM.

title: Adaptive Verification in vLLM: DSpark confidence-scheduled verification (blog)
quote: the last drafted token of a 7-token block survives less than 10% of the time
proves: On DeepSeek-V4-Pro (TP8, 8xB300), adaptive verification (PR #47808) keeps speculation beneficial up to concurrency 256 while fixed k>=5 loses; adds varlen decode CUDA graphs.
does_not_prove: Numbers only in figures; one large MoE model on top hardware; small-GPU regime not shown.
bearing: Strongly threatens 'spec hurts at high batch, fix by scheduling' ideas on big hardware.

title: DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation
quote: indiscriminately verifying these extended blocks wastes critical batch capacity on tokens with high rejection risks
proves: Per-request verification length from prefix survival probabilities and engine throughput profiles; 60-85% faster per-user generation at matched throughput vs MTP-1 in DeepSeek-V4 deployment.
does_not_prove: Production claim not independently reproduced; requires trained confidence head.
bearing: Same as B13/B14; the paper behind vLLM's adaptive verification.

title: Dynamic speculative decoding (vLLM v0.28.0 docs)
quote: DSD helps by tuning the K to an optimal value such that we continue to reap the benefits from SD.
proves: vLLM supports num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size: a static table of [start_bs, end_bs, K], K=0 allowed; auto-disabled with data parallelism; MRv1 piecewise cudagraph only.
does_not_prove: Static offline table, no per-request or acceptance feedback; no benchmark numbers; not verified whether present unchanged in vLLM 0.31.0 or vllm-metal.
bearing: Shows per-batch-size K and spec-off are already shipped; gap is per-request or memory-aware.

title: Adaptive speculative decoding (SGLang docs)
quote: Tier switch happens after the current round completes. Backends and CUDA graphs are never swapped mid-round.
proves: SGLang switches speculative_num_steps among tiers (default [1,3,7]) using an EMA (alpha 0.2) of batch-average accepted length, tracked per batch-size range; EAGLE/EAGLE3 with topk=1 only.
does_not_prove: Batch-level not per-request; no benchmark numbers; no hard spec-off at large batch.
bearing: Shows batch-level adaptive K is shipped in SGLang; per-request remains open there.

title: An Interpretable Latency Model for Speculative Decoding in LLM Serving
quote: explains why speedups often diminish as server load increases
proves: Analytical latency model fitted to vLLM measurements across drafter/verifier sizes, request rates, draft lengths and acceptance; explains shrinking speedup with load.
does_not_prove: Abstract gives no numbers; model, not a scheduler.
bearing: Supports using an analytic model to predict when spec should be off; threatens 'new cost model' novelty.

title: ECHO: Elastic Speculative Decoding with Sparse Gating for High-Concurrency Scenarios
quote: Existing evaluations typically overlook the compute-bound nature of high-concurrency regimes
proves: Budget-aware sparse gating reallocates tree verification budget across requests under high load; claims up to 5.35x walltime speedup and over 20% relative gain over SOTA.
does_not_prove: Venue not listed; 5.35x likely at low load; kernel compatibility details not checked.
bearing: Threatens cross-request verification budget ideas at high concurrency.

title: Semi-Clairvoyant Scheduling of Speculative Decoding Requests to Minimize LLM Inference Latency (LAPS-SD)
quote: LAPS-SD reduces inference latency by approximately 39% compared to state-of-the-art scheduling methods
proves: Request-level scheduler for SD that accounts for unpredictable acceptance-driven run times instead of output length alone; ~39% lower latency.
does_not_prove: Request ordering only; no admission against draft memory; baselines are schedulers, not SD controllers.
bearing: Threatens SD-aware request ordering ideas.

title: Adaptive Resource Allocation for Low-Latency LLM Serving (RIKEN AIP poster, Takamaeda team)
quote: Optimal aggressiveness of Speculative Decoding and Chunked Prefill depends on the request rate
proves: Jointly picks number of candidate tokens and chunked-prefill token budget to minimize TPOT under a TTFT constraint, on Vicuna 7B-33B, A100; dynamic beats any fixed setting.
does_not_prove: Poster only, no numbers in extracted text; title read from extracted PDF text; not peer reviewed.
bearing: Only source found on verification vs prefill token-budget sharing; supports that this joint area is thin.

title: FastGRPO: Accelerating Policy Optimization via Concurrency-aware Speculative Decoding and Online Draft Learning
quote: concurrency-aware speculative decoding framework that dynamically adjusts the drafting and verification strategy
proves: Direct SD in GRPO gives limited speedup at high concurrency; adapting draft/verify to live concurrency plus online draft learning gives 2.35x-2.72x end-to-end.
does_not_prove: Math reasoning only; no general serving admission.
bearing: Threatens 'spec as concurrency drops in RL rollout' ideas.

title: Fast LLM Post-training via Decoupled and Fastest-of-N Speculation (SpecActor)
quote: applying vanilla speculative decoding to rollout yields only 10 % speedup at worst on common production configurations
proves: At per-worker batch 128-256 (production GRPO/DAPO traces on 256 GPUs) vanilla SD gives no or negative gain; decoupled speculation plus Fastest-of-N drafts gives 2.0-2.4x mean rollout speed.
does_not_prove: Specific to RL rollout; batch shrinks during rollout, so gain concentrates in the tail.
bearing: Negative result for high-batch spec; supports tail-phase spec in rollouts.

title: Beat the long tail: Distribution-Aware Speculative Decoding for RL Training (DAS)
quote: reduces rollout time up to 50% while preserving identical training curves
proves: Suffix-tree drafter from recent rollouts plus length-aware policy that gives long trajectories larger draft budgets; up to 50% less rollout time.
does_not_prove: Nonparametric drafter only; no memory cost accounting of the suffix tree.
bearing: Threatens long-tail-aware spec budget ideas for rollouts.

title: History Rhymes: Accelerating LLM Reinforcement Learning with RhymeRL
venue: arXiv preprint (ASPLOS 26 per search, not on abs page)
quote: RhymeRL achieves a 2.6x performance improvement over existing methods
proves: HistoSpec drafts from prior-epoch rollouts; HistoPipe schedules using historical length distributions; 2.6x at dozens to thousands of GPUs.
does_not_prove: Needs a warm-up epoch (per B26); scheduling and spec gains not separated in abstract.
bearing: Threatens history-based rollout spec plus length-aware scheduling.

title: BubbleSpec: Turning Long-Tail Bubbles into Speculative Rollout Drafts for Synchronous Reinforcement Learning
quote: BubbleSpec reduces decoding steps by 50% and increases rollout throughput by up to 1.8x
proves: Uses idle time of fast DP ranks to pre-generate drafts for later steps; no warm-up epoch needed; up to 1.8x rollout throughput.
does_not_prove: Synchronous RL only; does not address serving.
bearing: Threatens idle-bubble draft generation ideas.

title: SPEC-RL: Accelerating On-Policy Reinforcement Learning with Speculative Rollouts
quote: SPEC-RL reduces rollout time by 2-3x without compromising policy quality
proves: Reuses prior-epoch trajectory segments as speculative prefixes; 2-3x rollout time reduction in PPO/GRPO/DAPO.
does_not_prove: Math benchmarks; draft source is history, not a model.
bearing: Crowds history-reuse rollout spec.

title: SRT: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning via Speculative Rollout with Tree-Structured Cache
quote: achieving up to 2.08x wall-clock time speedup during rollout
proves: Per-prompt tree cache of past continuations as model-free drafter, plus run-ahead generation in idle bubbles; up to 2.08x rollout speedup.
does_not_prove: Cache memory cost and eviction not described in abstract.
bearing: Crowds rollout spec; leaves draft-cache memory management open.

title: SPARK: Learning from Verification in Speculative GRPO Rollouts
quote: leverages target verification feedback to refine draft predictions during generation
proves: Draft misses repeat within a response and across a GRPO group; feeding verification back gives 32.7% over EAGLE3-style and 11.4% over DFlash-style generation speed, 21 settings.
does_not_prove: Drafter adaptation, not scheduling; gain over DFlash is modest.
bearing: Last-6-months check: rollout spec work is moving to drafter quality, not scheduling.
